label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences starting with e
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (96% of mass), i.e. when the model is about to output the first original token, and only for long sequences (L=8 or 9; nothing for L<=6). The strongest activations are when the first original token (the one being output) is e (80% of mass, 18x lift); t is a distant second. With L>=8 and first token e the predicate has ~96% precision and ~79% of activation mass. Weak tails it misses: low-magnitude delimiter activations on L=9 sequences with other first tokens (t, j, g, v, z...), and small pre-activations at the last original step (t=L-1) in the same e-initial long sequences. Does not fire during the copy phase or earlier in the original phase.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: e, t, j, g, v, z; least: 1, p, l, i) and the second original token (most: e, t, g, j, k, v; least: a, p, i, 1); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=8, L=9 & t=9.
